newsitem.title: FRANCE: Smaller groups could challenge for presidency.
newsitem.headline: Smaller groups could challenge for presidency.

text.p: Smaller groups in the European Parliament are considering submitting a joint candidate to challenge European People's Party (EPP) candidate Jose Maria Gil-Robles of Spain for the parliament's presidency.
The move is a reaction to the way the Socialists and the EPP, the parliament's two biggest groups, split the presidency between them.
"There are no hereditary rights for the Socialists and Conservatives for the post of EU parliament presidency," Claudia Roth, President of the parliament's Green Group said in a statement.
"It should be the turn of a candidate of a smaller group...The tradition of Socialists and Conservatives to share the presidency between them is deeply undemocratic."
The fact that the EPP chose Gil-Robles as its candidate means the assembly will be faced with an effective "fait accompli" when the vote is held in January.

Gil-Robles, a member of the Spanish Partido Popular, will succeed Klaus Haensch, a German Social Democrat, under a pact giving the 215-strong Socialist Group the first half of the five year term and the 182-strong EPP the second.

The Dutch leader of the parliament's Liberal Group, Gijs de Vries, also criticised the situation on Wednesday, admitting to reporters that the smaller groups were powerless to stop the two major groups.
